source_text.body:
Classify and reply to customer inquiries with an AI agent
A Make AI agent classifies form submissions (FAQ, quote, urgent, general), drafts a personalized reply, and pings Slack for emergencies; a separate module sends the email.
Done with
MK
Make
What they did
Susana Toth built a seven-module Make scenario around one AI Agent module. It had plain-English instructions, a 60-line FAQ file the agent searches, and a Slack tool for urgent cases. Gmail and SMTP weren't available as agent tools, so the agent writes the email text and a regular Email module sends it. She tested in the chat hub first.
How it went
The Small built-in model classified all four test cases correctly, with no mistakes. It cost 43–50 credits per run, against 42 for the Router and OpenAI version.
Worth knowing
Name and describe the Slack tool tightly, such as "only for urgent issues". Before she did, the agent pinged Slack on every inquiry.
Try it yourself
with
Make
Copy prompt
Build a Make scenario that triggers on each new submission from [your form tool], uses an AI agent to classify it as FAQ, quote request, urgent, or general, and drafts a personalized reply using my details: [business name, services, tone]. If it is urgent, post an alert to Slack channel [channel name]. Save every reply as a draft and pause to show me the email before any send step is turned on; you are done when a test submission of each type is routed correctly.
Original source: https://medium.com/@susanatoth-workflows/i-tested-make-coms-new-ai-agents-on-a-live-workflow-here-s-what-it-actually-costs-6fbf03d02e8e
